title: SPARTACUS - PROSPECTIVE MULTICENTER STUDY TO DESCRIBE CHARACTERISTICS OF PRETREATED OR TREATMENT-NAIVE FARICIMAB PATIENTS WITH NAMD/DME AND TO EVALUATE EFFECTIVENESS AND DURABILITY OF FARICIMAB IN A GERMAN REAL-WORLD COHORT
summary:
The SPARTACUS study is an observational study conducted in Germany. It focuses on two common eye conditions: neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD) and diabetic macular edema (DME). In both diseases, abnormal leaking blood vessels lead to fluid accumulation in and under the retina, causing visual impairment and potentially leading to vision loss if left untreated.

Intravitreal operative drug administration (IVOM)—in which an ophthalmologist injects the medication directly into the vitreous body of the eye—is currently an important treatment option for nAMD and DME. Various medications are used in therapy. Currently, however, there are insufficient prospective real-world data describing the functional and anatomical outcomes of this patient group following a switch to the active substance faricimab or upon initiating first-line treatment with faricimab.

The goal of the study is to determine how effectively faricimab works under routine clinical conditions—that is, outside of strictly controlled laboratory settings—following a treatment switch from bevacizumab or from ranibizumab or aflibercept 2 mg. In addition, data from patients who initiated faricimab therapy as first-line treatment will be evaluated.

The study investigates whether the medication reduces retinal fluid and thus central subfield thickness, whether vision is maintained or improved, and whether it can contribute to better disease control and a reduction in treatment burden. Since this is a purely observational study, no additional tests or experiments are performed on the patients. Physicians simply collect data over a 12-month period from standard routine examinations, such as the results of visual acuity tests and specialized eye scans (OCT).

interventions.name:
Arm A: Patients who received 3–7 injections of bevacizumab before switching to faricimab due to an insufficient response. A total of 233 patients with nAMD and 50 patients with DME will be enrolled in this arm.

Applies to all arms:
Each patient will be observed for 12 months after initiating far

Arm B: Patients treated with ranibizumab or aflibercept 2 mg as their sole prior therapy before switching to faricimab. A total of 233 patients with nAMD and 50 patients with DME will be enrolled in this arm.
Arm C: Patients who initiated faricimab therapy as first-line treatment. A total of 180 patients with nAMD and 18 patients with DME will be enrolled in this arm.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
General Inclusion Criteria (All Arms):
The inclusion criteria apply only to the study eye:

• Diagnosis of nAMD or DME
• Age: ≥ 40 years at the time of study enrollment
• At least one intravitreal faricimab injection at the time of enrollment
• Visual acuity (VA) of the study eye between 30 and 80 ETDRS letters (0.08 to 0.8 Snellen decimal visual acuity) at the initiation of the first faricimab administration
• For retrospective data: Availability of OCT and visual acuity prior to the start of faricimab treatment (baseline date) and after the third faricimab injection
• The patient or the patient's legal representative has signed the informed consent form

Specific Inclusion Criteria for Pretreated Patients in Arms A and B (Switched Patients):

Arm A (Bevacizumab):

Pre-baseline data:
• Availability of OCT and visual acuity prior to the start of bevacizumab treatment (pre-baseline)
Reason for switch:
• Insufficient anatomical response (i.e., persistent, recurrent, or worsening retinal fluid) to bevacizumab therapy

Number of injections:
• Three to seven intravitreal bevacizumab injections prior to switching to faricimab therapy

Arm B (Ranibizumab/Aflibercept 2 mg):

Pre-baseline data:
• Availability of OCT and visual acuity prior to the start of treatment with ranibizumab or aflibercept 2 mg (pre-baseline)
Exclusion criteria:
General Exclusion Criteria (All Arms):
The exclusion criteria apply only to the study eye:

• Prior treatment with photodynamic therapy or retinal laser therapy in the center of the eye (delimited by the vascular arches)
• Prior treatment with steroids
• More than 4 months on faricimab therapy
• Other retinal/intraocular diseases (e.g., secondary choroidal neovascularization [CNV], uveitis, trauma, inflammatory diseases, myopia > -6 diopters, angioid streaks, vision-impairing cataract) that, in the opinion of the treating physician, could affect visual acuity in the study eye
• Current participation in another ophthalmological interventional and/or non-interventional study
• Pregnant and/or breastfeeding individuals

Specific Exclusion Criteria for Pretreated Patients in Arms A and B (Switched Patients):

Arm A (Bevacizumab):

Prior treatment:
• Prior treatment with anti-VEGF agents other than bevacizumab before switching to faricimab
Duration of prior treatment:
• More than 12 months on bevacizumab therapy

Arm B (Ranibizumab/Aflibercept 2 mg):

Prior treatment:
• Prior treatment with anti-VEGF agents other than either ranibizumab or aflibercept 2 mg as sole prior therapy before switching to faricimab
